record.paper_title: Nuclei of Seyfert galaxies and QSOs - Central engine & conditions of star formation: Workshop summary and open questions
record.original_question: What is the structure of the broad-line region in active galactic nuclei, and how is that line-emitting region connected to toroidal obscuration by a clumpy medium or molecular torus around the central black hole?

evidence.quote: He also showed that in the handful of sources where the velocity resolved RM has been applied, the broad line region (BLR) geometry displays a disk-like structure and signs of infall from the hydrogen-emission lines.
A key element in the unified model is the torus, whose nature and appearance are still unknown.
4. What is the structure of the broad line region (BLR) and how is it connected to the toroidal obscuration?

The connection of the BLR with the toroidal obscuration seems to be regulated by the AGN continuum as it interacts with a clumpy medium, and with the molecular torus existing beyond a certain radius (of sublimation) from the central mass black hole.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In an active galactic nucleus (AGN), the broad-line region (BLR) is the region of fast-moving photoionized gas surrounding the central supermassive black hole that produces Doppler-broadened permitted emission lines (e.g., the hydrogen Balmer lines), while the obscuring "torus" refers to the circumnuclear distribution of dust and gas, situated beyond the dust sublimation radius, that is invoked in unified models to absorb and reprocess radiation from the central engine into the infrared.

Determine the geometric and kinematic structure of the BLR (e.g., its spatial distribution, degree of flattening or disk-like character, presence of inflow/outflow components, and dependence on luminosity and emission line) and characterize how the BLR is physically connected to the toroidal obscuring medium. Specifically:

(a) Provide a model for the BLR consistent with velocity-resolved reverberation-mapping signatures, including disk-like geometry and possible infall.

(b) Specify the structure of the obscuring torus (smooth versus clumpy, equatorial disk versus polar component, inner radius set by dust sublimation).

(c) Describe the transition between the BLR and the torus: how the AGN ionizing continuum interacts with a clumpy medium, and how the molecular torus beyond the sublimation radius merges with or feeds the inner line-emitting clouds.
artifact.category_tag: AGN broad-line region and torus structure
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature (through 2024) continues to investigate the BLR–torus connection without a settled model. Reviews and observational studies indicate the obscuring medium is clumpy, dynamic, and may include both equatorial and polar components, and that the BLR and inner dusty torus may form a continuous radially extended structure straddling the sublimation radius. Cloud-obscuration events (e.g., in EC 04570–5206) and reverberation-mapping results support disk-like BLR geometry with inflow signatures, but a unified quantitative model remains an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Nuclear obscuration in active galactic nuclei (Nature Astronomy)
status_evidence.snippet: The structure of this circumnuclear material is found to be complex, clumpy and dynamic ... consists of two structures: an equatorial disk/torus and a polar component.
status_evidence.claim: The torus structure remains under active investigation and is known to be clumpy, with multiple components.

status_evidence.title: eROSITA detection of a cloud obscuration event in the Seyfert AGN EC 04570–5206 (A&A 2024)
status_evidence.snippet: transiting gas clouds ... lower limits on their radial distances are commensurate with the dust sublimation zone or the optical broad line region
status_evidence.claim: Recent 2024 observations continue to probe the BLR–torus interface via clumpy obscuration events, indicating the question is still open.

status_evidence.title: Broad Line AGN: Structure and Dynamics
status_evidence.snippet: BLR structures and dusty-torus structures may comprise one continuous, radially extended structure straddling both inside and outside the dust sublimation zone
status_evidence.claim: Current models propose, but have not established, that BLR and torus form a continuous structure.
